sections.title: 34.1 Why can't I clone an unknown quantum state?

content.explanation: Assume U exists such that U|ψ⟩|0⟩ = |ψ⟩|ψ⟩. For two states, ⟨ψ|φ⟩ = ⟨ψ|φ⟩², which implies the inner product is 0 or 1 – a contradiction for arbitrary states. Physical reason: linearity of QM.

content.statement: Measurement collapses the superposition to an eigenstate.
content.explanation: Before: |ψ⟩ = (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2. After: |0⟩ or |1⟩. Interference requires coherent superposition; measurement destroys coherence.
content.example: Double‑slit interference disappears when a detector is placed at the slits.
keyTakeaways: Measurement collapses the superposition to an eigenstate.

sections.title: 34.3 What does phase actually mean physically?

content.statement: Relative phase affects interference; global phase is unobservable.
content.explanation: Global phase e^{iθ}|ψ⟩ is unobservable. Relative phase in |ψ⟩ = (|0⟩ + e^{iφ}|1⟩)/√2 affects measurement outcomes in different bases. Example: φ=0 → |+⟩; φ=π → |−⟩.
keyTakeaways: Relative phase affects interference; global phase is unobservable.

sourceAudit.sourceTitle: 34.3 What does phase actually mean physically?

content.statement: Unitarity preserves probability and inner products.
content.explanation: U†U = I ensures that ⟨ψ|U†U|ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ = 1, so probabilities sum to 1. It also makes evolution reversible, conserving information.
content.example: Hadamard H is unitary: H†H = I.
keyTakeaways: Unitarity preserves probability and inner products.
